fit: potato menu options and ordinal OFF categories in a Parkinson diet comparison
assessment: Both self-selected diet groups could eat potatoes. Tables 5 and 6 give cross-sectional ordinal waking-day OFF distributions with baseline imbalance and inconclusive four-week arm difference (Fisher p=.054). Preparation-specific intake and individual OFF times were not reported.

fit: weighed cold potato salad in a standardized Parkinson lunch
assessment: Cold potato salad consumed averaged 232 g among 21 advanced Parkinson participants versus 291 g among 20 early Parkinson participants. Participants received the same mixed meal and were assessed in the ON state. The outcome is food intake, without a roasted-potato comparison or daily OFF duration.

fit: daytime protein comparison with clinical motor fluctuation outcomes
assessment: Seven of eight motor fluctuators showed immediate improvement with a low-protein menu. This selected clinical series with a hospital meal comparison varied overall protein and reported clinical control, not daily OFF hours from potatoes. Participant overlap with the later Pincus and Barry series is unresolved.

fit: depleted Syrian oregano stems in a bay leaf trial comparator
assessment: The 25-person Origanum syriacum stem comparator changed from 50.32 to 50.76 on the paper's STAI measure (reported p=.8846). The study compared it with bay leaf and did not include a no-oregano comparator. Species, plant part, depletion and population limit transfer to culinary dried oregano in Parkinson disease.

fit: dried oregano leaf infusion and motor-confounded mouse exploration
assessment: Leaf infusion reduced mouse hole exploration at 750 and 1000 mg/kg; the higher dose also impaired motor coordination in rotarod and chimney tasks. Sedation or motor impairment confounds behavioral interpretation, and no clinical anxiety was measured.
